name: Kona (Dilshad Nahar Kona)

global_influences.artist_or_genre: Contemporary pop / electronic-fusion production (via Fuad al Muqtadir collaborations)
global_influences.evidence: Kona's collaborations with producer Fuad al Muqtadir (e.g., 'Fuad featuring Kona') placed her classically trained voice within electronic/fusion pop production, mirroring the broader Habib Wahid-style folk-electronic fusion trend in Bangladeshi pop.
global_influences.source: Wikipedia Dilshad Nahar Kona; TheAudioDB artist profile

local_adaptation_notes: Trained in Nazrul Geeti at Nazrul Academy and formerly a member of the girl group Angels Four, Kona transitioned to a solo pop career with her 2006 debut Jamtika Bhalobasha (soft pop under Laser Vision), later blending her classical training with contemporary electronic-pop production through collaborations with Fuad al Muqtadir — illustrating the classical-training-to-pop-fusion pipeline common among female Bangladeshi pop vocalists of her generation.
sound_evolution_summary: Formative period: classical training in Nazrul Geeti; early group experience in Angels Four. Solo breakthrough (2006): debut album Jamtika Bhalobasha introduced her as a soft-pop solo vocalist. Later period: extensive film playback career (Chorabali, 2012; Kacher Shatru, 2014; Warning, 2015; Bishwoshundori, 2020) culminating in the Bangladesh National Film Award for Best Female Playback Singer (2020), alongside pop-fusion collaborations (Fuad featuring Kona, Simply Kona).

listener_community_notes: Bridges classically trained vocal audiences and mainstream pop/film listeners; National Film Award recognition (2020) signals sustained mainstream industry standing within the Pop genre.
